title: Does the cold-start insight for direct air capture survive exergy accounting? A negative result for our hypothesis, with a certified surrogate and a Lean core
description:
McDannald et al. (NIST; arXiv 2501.04825) define an intrinsic capture efficiency ξ = ΔnCO2/Etotal for a sorbent in an idealised piston cycle and conclude that it is greatly beneficial to start cold. Their Etotal is a face-value sum of heats and works: the return step is set to zero and no ambient temperature appears. We asked whether the conclusion survives when every heat is weighted by its Carnot factor against an explicit ambient temperature T0, sub-ambient cooling is priced by refrigeration, and the return step is charged. Our preregistered hypothesis was that it would not (prior 0.35); it is refuted. For all 14 Pareto rows of their Table 2 the exergy-optimal start temperature, found by a joint grid over T1, ΔT and Pend, lies between 200 and 236.5 K in every one of 18 variants (T0 = 273.15, 298.15, 313.15 K; three heat-recovery levels; with and without a purity constraint). The benefit of a cold start shrinks (best ξ with a cold start over best ξ with T1 ≥ 298.15 K: face value 10 to 819, exergy without recovery 3.5 to 129, with full reversible recovery 1.25 to 6.6) but stays above 1. Exergy-weighted efficiencies on the stored paths are 25.4 to 36.8 μmol/J against 5.98 to 11.26 at face value (nominal recomputation; printed posterior means 6.12 to 11.259). The published ξ never exceeds 1/Wmin of the ideal mixture; five dataset entries (CSMNOX, GUSNEN, PACYIE, SABWAU01, UJOKIP05) have heat flows inconsistent with the second law, read as inconsistent inputs in those entries. On a seeded sample of 150 materials the exergy optimum moves to T1 ≥ T0 in 3 of 150 (conditional slice scan). The paper includes a step-by-step account for readers outside adsorption engineering.

Tier split. Tier A (Lean 4.34.1, Mathlib; axioms within propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): the twelve theorems of DacExergy/Core.lean, which are real-number algebra (Carnot weights in (0,1), a factorisation, sign and threshold equivalences, positivity and monotonicity of RT0 ln(1/x)); planted sorry and planted axiom controls are caught by the axiom audit; no statement lock, no independent recompile yet. Tier L: the source paper's model (eqs. 1 to 10, Table 2) and the dataset and code licences, taken as stated (data: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14452152, CC-BY-4.0; code: NIST IntrinsicDACCycle v0.0.2, NIST software licence; credited fully, not redistributed). Tier C: closed-form survival conditions (an N2 threshold and a heat-capacity threshold) and mpmath-interval enclosures about a stylised two-component surrogate only; the surrogate disagrees with the full model on most Table 2 rows at full heat recovery. Tier X: the full-model re-accounting, the grid scans, the sample and the dataset-wide checks.

Controls. Positive: Table 2 reproduced in 14 of 14 rows to the printed digits and stored terms to 3.8e-11 before any re-weighting; an all-T ≥ T0 path has weights in (0,1) and no refrigeration term. Negative, all rejected by our consistency gate: double-counted sorbent heat, a planted x106 unit error, the text's 1.0 x 105 mol/J taken literally, and heats of adsorption removed. The unit sentence in the source is consistent with 1.0 x 10-5 mol/J (a typesetting matter; table and data are self-consistent).

What this is NOT. These are thermodynamic limits of a published simplified model (idealised piston, Henry/IAST loadings, binary CO2/N2 air, no water). The paper is not a statement about real plants, costs, sorbent performance in practice or any climate effect, and makes no recommendation. It does not say the NIST metric or its authors are wrong; face value and exergy are two accounting conventions.

Limitations. The supplement of the source was not obtained and not read; no independent audit (human or AI) exists, no statement lock, GATE-1 adequacy checks not run; the advisor review timed out; repository guards were not run; the joint search is a grid with refinement, with a substituted cell mass; no author contact. Observations about the published code and data (unseeded posterior draws, three descriptions of the single path, eight rows with P1 below 101,325 Pa, grid paths that exceed several published rows, so the published front may not be fully converged) are stated as observations to check, not claims.
